articles.title: Traders brought Central American cacao to Georgia 1,000 years ago
articles.desc: A thousand years ago, feasts in what’s now northern Georgia (in the US) included cacao from Central America. Potsherds discarded after an 11th-century feast at Etowah—an Indigenous city just north of what’s now Atlanta, Georgia—contained traces of cacao, a raw ingredient of chocolate. The chemical residue and ancient DNA reveal that not only did the Mississippian people who built the city have excellent taste, they also had trade connections that reached at least 3,000 kilometers to Central America. articles.title: Ratko Mladić, ‘butcher of Bosnia’, dies at the Hague aged 84
articles.desc: Ratko Mladić, the former Bosnian Serb military commander who was the architect of the 1995 Srebrenica massacre during the Bosnian War, has died aged 84, according to Serbian state media . articles.title: Innovative etching method for silicon: Higher precision through interlayer
articles.desc: In micro- and nanotechnology, highly precise components with tall, narrow structures (high aspect ratios) made from semiconductor materials like silicon are important. A promising fabrication method is gas-phase metal-assisted chemical etching (MacEtch). In this plasma-free process, a thin metal layer defines the pattern on the silicon substrate. The etching step takes place in a chemical environment, where the reaction occurs only at the interface between the metal and silicon. The metal catalyst gradually sinks into the silicon, directing the etching deeper.

articles.title: How plants use scoop-shaped pores to distribute their pollen efficiently

articles.title: Permafrost thaws worldwide as active layers deepen from 2000 to 2024
articles.desc: An international study led by researchers at the George Washington University indicates clear global evidence that permafrost is thawing across much of the planet. The findings confirm that permafrost degradation accelerated globally between 2000 and 2024.

articles.title: Congo Basin study reveals nuanced relationship between people and flooding
articles.desc: In the Lac Télé Community Reserve, a vast tropical peatland in Africa's Congo Basin that is home to about 20,000 people, the forces of climate change and globalization are hitting residents hard. Wer schon mal im Ausland zum Essen ausgegangen ist, weiß: Beim Trinkgeld gelten dort oft andere Regeln als zu Hause. Was deutsche Urlauber als angemessen oder großzügig empfinden, kann anderswo befremdlich wirken – oder sogar als unhöflich gelten. Deshalb lohnt es sich, vor einer Reise einen Blick auf die lokalen Gepflogenheiten zu werfen. In Deutschland läuft es meist ungefähr so ab. Der Ausdruck ist dabei mehr als ein Hinweis aufs bald anstehende Mittagessen: Er fungiert als lockere Grußformel unter Kolleginnen und Kollegen und signalisiert oft den Übergang von der Arbeit in die Pause.
